sentences.text: The holotype specimen — the specific fossil used to define the species — includes a skull, lower jaw, and nine neck vertebrae.
The first preserved neck bone, known as the axis, has a central body measuring 16.3 cm in length, while the tenth vertebra measures 19.9 cm.
This specimen was discovered in 2007 in Jiudu Village, Lufeng County, Yunnan Province, China.
The genus name Lishulong translates to "chestnut tree dragon," combining Chinese words for the tree and a mythical creature, while the species name wangi honors paleontologist Wang Zheng-Ju.
Fragments of the posterior skeleton were found but were lost during the excavation process.
The fossil site is near where the theropod dinosaur Panguraptor was discovered.
Phylogenetic analysis places Lishulong within the Sauropodiformes as the sister taxon to Yunnanosaurus.
Lishulong lived approximately between 199 and 183 million years ago, spanning the Sinemurian to Toarcian stages, though estimates range from 199.5 to 174.7 million years ago.
